question: A man sold an article for ₹216, there by gaining 20%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

20% gain in fractional form = 20 ÷ 100 = 1 ÷ 5

Let Cost Price (CP) = 5 units and Profit = 1 unit

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 5 + 1 = 6 units

6 units = ₹216 ⇒ 1 unit = 216 ÷ 6 = 36

Cost Price (CP) = 5 units = 5 × 36 = 180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the article = ₹216

Gain percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)] × SP

 
 
 CP
 ?
 
 
 
 SP
 ₹216
 
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 +20% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 + 20)] × 216

⇒ CP = (100 ÷ 120) × 216

⇒ CP = (5 ÷ 6) × 216

⇒ CP = 5 × 36

⇒ CP = 180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than Cost Price, a loss is incurred. Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit or Discount

For two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b ÷ 100).
